health_and_wellness.summary: Health-conscious and structured, with yoga, walking, modified jogging, strength work, and medical adherence.
details: Practices Vinyasa yoga about three times weekly and uses movement for stress and body maintenance (Q15, Q31, Q50).
Manages mild high blood pressure with diet, exercise, and prescribed medication (Q31, Q33, Q39).
Uses physical therapy exercises and modified running due to knee pain (Q33, Q34).
Reports anxiety tendencies around control and responsibility, showing up as tight chest, over-checking schedules, and replaying conversations, without a formal diagnosis (Q45).
Does not smoke, drinks lightly about two or three times a month or less, and does not use marijuana or other substances (Q38, Q39).
Uses Ayurvedic and home remedies such as ginger-tulsi tea, turmeric, honey, and ajwain steam alongside regular medical care, not as substitutes for serious conditions (Q37).
Is pro-vaccine and sees COVID vaccines, boosters, flu shots, and childhood vaccinations as a responsibility in food service and around older people (Q41).

During a stressful week involving her father's diabetes scare, work shortages, and Maya's college deadlines, she accepted support from Nisha and Rajesh rather than trying to handle everything perfectly (Q44).

food_and_dining.summary: Highly food-centered, blending Gujarati home cooking, Indian-fusion creativity, and professional food safety discipline.
details: Cooks dal, rice, vegetables, chutneys, tandoori salmon, quinoa biryani, and seasonal Indian-fusion meals (Q05, Q17, Q108).
Shops at Costco, Kroger, Patel Brothers, and local Indian markets for fresh produce, spices, and staples (Q08, Q57).
Values aesthetic plating and farm-to-table style cooking (Q108, Q109).
Uses Sunday bulk prep such as chopped onions, cooked dal, washed greens, marinated protein, quinoa or rice, roasted vegetables, chutney, and tandoori salmon marinade to reduce takeout (Q17).
Uses pantry meals such as dal, rice, khichdi, chana, vegetable pulao, and soups to stretch money during tighter months (Q81).

travel.summary: Culturally immersive travel is a major aspiration, especially India and food-centered international destinations.
details: Maintains family ties in Gujarat and hopes to visit India again in the next few years (Q62, Q86).
Wants future travel to India, Italy, Japan, and Morocco (Q108).
Maintains a separate travel fund to protect travel savings from routine expenses (Q61).
Would delay travel or eating out when health care, dental, physical therapy, or other necessary costs rise (Q40, Q60).

social_and_relationships.summary: Strong family-centered and community-linked social life, with close ties to spouse, children, parents, brother, friends, coworkers, dance group, and yoga circle.
details: Lives with husband Rajesh and teenage children Maya and Neel (Q05, Q51).
Relies on friend Nisha, dance group, yoga class, community organization, and work friends Carla and Minh (Q07, Q44).
Sees brother Amit and nearby parents regularly and shares elder care responsibilities (Q06, Q35).
Her father has diabetes and heart issues, her mother has arthritis, and she helps with appointments and food while Amit helps with driving and paperwork (Q35).
Rajesh's parents live in New Jersey and support for them is mostly by phone or WhatsApp (Q05, Q35).
Family stress patterns include Rajesh worrying quietly about money and his parents, Maya feeling college pressure, and Neel getting moody when school and sports pile up (Q46).
The family copes with stress through meals together, walks, and occasional no-phone dinners (Q46).

home_and_lifestyle.summary: Organized suburban homeowner with a disciplined calendar, shared household finances, and practical routines.
details: Owns a home with a mortgage in Farmington and lives in a stable four-person household (Q08, Q11, Q58).
Uses spreadsheets, folders, phone reminders, and Sunday meal prep to manage family life (Q15, Q17, Q75).
Maintains a small herb garden with cilantro, mint, basil, and curry leaf pots (Q17).

Permanent household is four people; mother occasionally stays overnight and relatives may visit during weddings or festival weekends, but no relatives, lodgers, boarders, or employees live there full time (Q12-Q14, Q51-Q54).
Rajesh and Shoba share household expenses; she mostly manages bills while Rajesh handles the mortgage and larger planning (Q55).
Typical monthly spending is about $6,000 to $6,300, with a higher recent month around $6,800 due to dental and school costs; groceries usually run about $1,000 to $1,200 (Q56-Q57).
Together Rajesh and Shoba made about $9,200 gross and about $6,700 take-home last month; Shoba's own gross pay was about $4,400 and take-home about $3,200 (Q72-Q74).
Current household debts are the mortgage and one car loan; credit cards are normally paid off monthly and there are no student loans, family loans, or long-term medical debt (Q63).
Household does not receive SNAP, housing vouchers, SSI, or similar public benefits (Q80).
Could cover a $400 emergency from savings or checking, though several emergencies together might require deeper savings use or temporary credit card use (Q82).
Seasonal expenses rise with winter utilities, school costs in August and September, Diwali/festival spending in October and November, and December travel or gift costs (Q59).
Copes with extra expenses by using savings, cutting restaurants and clothing, delaying wants such as furniture, taking occasional overtime, and cooking cheaper pantry meals (Q60, Q81).

summaries.demographer: Shoba Mehta is a 51-year-old married Indian-American woman living in Farmington, Michigan with her husband and two teenage children (Q05, Q51, Q85). She was born in Detroit to Gujarati immigrant parents and grew up in Farmington Hills in a bilingual, Hindu, family-centered household (Q86, Q87, Q97). She has some college education, no bachelor's degree, and works full time as a food service supervisor in a healthcare dining operation (Q90, Q65). Her household is stable, homeowner, dual-income, and middle-class but still exposed to college, healthcare, and elder-care pressures (Q58, Q74, Q83).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Shoba shows high planning orientation, loss aversion around debt, and strong future discounting discipline through spreadsheets, emergency savings, college accounts, and separate travel funds (Q61, Q62, Q75). Her spending choices reveal identity-based utility: she cuts restaurants and furniture before health, education, good spices, festivals, and meaningful travel (Q59, Q60, Q83). She responds to uncertainty with routines, lists, savings buffers, and skill-building rather than risk-taking (Q15, Q61, Q82). Peer and family norms matter, but she filters them through practicality, as seen in her career crossroads and cautious restaurant ambitions (Q02, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: Shoba is a regular voter and moderate Democrat who is closer to the Democratic Party because of healthcare, education, civil rights, immigration, reproductive rights, and inclusion (Q23, Q95, Q96). Her politics are pragmatic rather than ideological, shaped by working in food service, being the child of immigrants, and seeing essential workers' conditions during the pandemic (Q24, Q25). She has moderate institutional trust: she supports accountable policing, reliable public health sources, and local civic participation while remaining skeptical of slogans and misinformation (Q27, Q42, Q48). Her civic life is strongest through community organizations, cultural festivals, food drives, and local elections (Q17, Q23, Q47).
summaries.psychologist: Shoba presents as conscientious, organized, socially embedded, achievement-oriented, and emotionally responsible, with a strong identity built around hospitality, competence, culture, and family duty (Q01, Q15, Q109). She acknowledges anxiety tendencies around control and responsibility but uses adaptive coping strategies such as yoga, walking, prayer, lists, painting, and trusted conversations (Q43, Q45, Q50). Her relational style is supportive but high-accountability, visible in family caregiving, kitchen supervision, and community volunteering (Q35, Q65, Q07). Her self-concept integrates practicality and ambition: she accepts constraints while continuing to pursue management, culinary education, and creative food goals (Q02, Q108).
